question: Should adoption of explicit descendant output by requester orchestration count as terminal delivery proof even when the requester's later outward send fails?
rationale: The patch can mechanically record this state, but only maintainers can choose whether internal requester consumption or successful outward delivery is the permanent product boundary that suppresses descendant retries.

options.title: Accept consumption after proof
options.body: Treat narrowly matched requester consumption as terminal delivery proof after real restart evidence confirms consumed rows settle and unconsumed rows remain retryable.

options.title: Require outward delivery
options.body: Credit descendants only after the requester result is successfully delivered outward, preserving retry behavior when the final send fails.

options.title: Use durable inbox semantics
options.body: Pause this branch and resolve consumption, retries, and final outward delivery together in the broader durable completion inbox or spool design.

recommendation.title: Accept consumption after proof
recommendation.body: Treat narrowly matched requester consumption as terminal delivery proof after real restart evidence confirms consumed rows settle and unconsumed rows remain retryable.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects them to the central cron, lifecycle, and persisted registry paths affected by this semantic choice.
